chunks: And regarding what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari from Zur'a from Sama'ah from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him about fasting three days in the month, so he said: In every ten days, Thursday, Wednesday, and Thursday; and in the following month, Wednesday, Thursday, and Wednesday. This does not contradict the earlier reports because the person is free to choose between fasting Wednesday between two Thursdays, or fasting Thursday between two Wednesdays. Whichever he acts upon is permissible, as indicated by that.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended schedule for fasting three days in each month according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the fiqh of the 'Ayyam al-Beed' (white days) by offering two flexible patterns—either Wednesday-Thursday-Wednesday or Thursday-Wednesday-Thursday—resolving apparent contradictions in earlier reports by affirming the believer's choice. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease and adaptability in voluntary worship, ensuring that strict adherence to one sequence does not invalidate the spiritual merit of the other. This flexibility underscores the principle that the intention and consistency of fasting are paramount over rigid calendrical constraints.
